errorCodes.meaning: The domain does not accept self-registration by invite.
The domain already holds the most pending invites the service allows. Revoke unused ones, or wait for them to expire.
The submitted `domain` is not a known hosting domain on this consumer. See [the category conventions](../../../../_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md#2-unknown-domain-error).

AccountInvite.description: An invite to register an account, as the issuing service describes it. Never carries the invite's token or claim code, which are returned once, by did-management/account/invite/issue.

createdBy.description: The DID of the administrator who issued it.

domain.description: The hosting domain the invite admits an account on.

expiresAt.description: The last instant the invite can be redeemed.

inviteId.description: The service's identifier for the invite. Not a secret: knowing it does not let anyone redeem the invite.

label.description: The issuer's note on who the invite is for. Operator-facing; never shown to the invitee by this task family.

pathPrefix.description: When present, the account's DIDs must be hosted under this path prefix, in addition to any rule the domain sets. Absent: the domain's rules alone apply.

redeemedAt.description: When it was redeemed. Present exactly when `state` is `redeemed`.

redeemedBy.description: The account subject that redeemed it. Present exactly when `state` is `redeemed`.

referral.description: The referral the administrator recorded on the invite. An account the invite admits carries it as verified.

state.description: `pending`: redeemable. `redeemed`: an account was registered with it. `revoked`: withdrawn before use. `expired`: `expiresAt` passed before use.

AccountInvite.title: AccountInvite

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

Referral.description: How a self-registered account came to the service, as attribution: who sent it (`via`) and a free-text note (`label`). Never authority — a service MUST NOT authorise anything on it.

label.description: A short note on the source — a campaign, an invitation's origin. Free text, never interpreted.

via.description: The DID of the party that sent the registrant, usually a trust community. Absent when only a `label` was given.

Referral.title: Referral

Response.description: The issued invite and, once only, its two secrets. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

claimCode.description: A short code the invitee presents with the token. The administrator delivers it over a different channel from the token, so that intercepting one is not enough to redeem. Returned only here; the service keeps a slow hash of it.

token.description: The invite's single-use token, of at least 128 bits of entropy. Returned only here; the service keeps a slow hash of it.

schema.description: An administrator of a DID hosting service issues a single-use invite that lets a party with no account register one (did-management/account/register). The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

domain.description: The hosting domain the invite admits an account on. The domain must accept self-registration by invite.

label.description: An operator note on who the invite is for, shown by did-management/account/invite/list. Never sent to the invitee by this family.

pathPrefix.description: When present, the account's DIDs must be hosted under this path prefix, in addition to the domain's own path rules. Absent: the domain's rules alone apply.

referral.description: Optional: the source this invite stands for (a community, a campaign). The account it admits carries this referral as verified, in place of any the registrant states.

ttlSeconds.description: How long the invite stays redeemable, in seconds (at most 30 days). REQUIRED, with no default: how long an unredeemed invite may wait is the operator's policy. A consumer MAY cap it lower.
